# Log vectors: <label> <address> <topics> <data> <rlp>
# topics is comma-separated hex, `-` when there are none; data is hex, `-`
# when empty. All hex is without 0x.
#
# TWO SOURCES, AND THE LABEL SAYS WHICH.
#
#   corpus-*  OCTETS THAT SHIPPED IN A BLOCK. ethereum/execution-specs
#             release tests@v20.0.1 (2026-07-15), asset fixtures.tar.gz.
#             A receipt publishes its logs and its own RLP together, and
#             element 3 of that RLP is the encoded log list.
#
#   the rest  Constructed, and encoded by the executable specification
#             itself (execution-specs @ tests@v20.0.1, 87aba1a38) -- never
#             by this project. They cover shapes no corpus row reaches.
#
# EVERY CORPUS ROW WAS CROSS-VERIFIED BEFORE BEING WRITTEN: element 3 was
# sliced out of the receipt's own octets, the fixture's separately-decoded
# JSON fields were re-encoded by an implementation independent of the one
# under test, and the two were required to agree. Corpus-wide: 2193
# receipts carry logs, 2193 verified, 0 slice mismatches,
# 0 bloom mismatches.
#
# WHAT THE CORPUS DOES NOT REACH, which is why the constructed rows stay:
# five topics (no opcode emits one, so the corpus holds 0 through 4), the
# exact 55/56-byte RLP form boundary, and the fixed-width extremes.
#
# A DECLARED CAP, not a silent one: the corpus's widest log data is
# 9,177,456 bytes and a row carrying it would be 18 MB of unreviewable hex.
# Corpus rows are capped at 512 bytes of data; 3011 log entries were
# dropped by that cap, and the widest corpus entry surviving it carries
# 241 bytes.
#
# TWO SELECTIONS RAN, AND THE SECOND IS THE NARROWER ONE. After the cap,
# rows were chosen to cover distinct (topic-count, data-width) shapes:
# 56 shapes were found and 24 kept. That shape selection, not the cap,
# is what decides the widths actually written here -- the widest CORPUS
# row in this file carries 4 bytes of data, and the widest row of any
# kind carries 300 (a constructed one). Reading 241 as this file's
# widest row overstates its data coverage by about sixtyfold.
